findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. On this alone a newcomer could say what the project is and why it matters.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: a clone command, prerequisites, one setup command and a sample request, with a note on what `athena ask` acts on. There is also a link near the top that jumps straight here.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, check that you have these prerequisites" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The only section that would show Athena's own output (models, verdict, cost) is the first section after the nav, and it shows an error. A newcomer's first look at the product's promise is a failure message, and nothing else on the page shows a real Athena job.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Almost all of the page explains a different project, firstmate, through states, transitions, a glossary and 45 claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out from the third lede paragraph that this whole page is only a sample of Athena's output.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks..."

findings.text: The page never says which models Athena uses, what accounts or API keys it needs, or roughly what a run costs. The prerequisites only mention "Claude Code, or npm to install it", which leaves the cost and access question open.
findings.source: "It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: This link in the header is meant for the project owner. A newcomer has no context for it, and it sits right next to the newcomer's "Next step" link.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate explanation is careful and honest about its sources, but it is dense. Several glossary entries say the source does not define the term, and terms like "exit 75", "guarded fast-forward" and "pending-close record" assume the reader knows git and shell. A newcomer will get the gist of firstmate but will struggle with the details.
findings.source: Words used first: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."; Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake

findings.text: This closing section talks about the repository's internal layout, which means nothing to a first-time visitor. It does not tell them anything they can act on.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
